what_its_for: Methotrexate is used to treat certain types of cancer, severe rheumatoid arthritis (painful, swollen joints), severe psoriasis (thick, scaly skin patches), and some other conditions where the immune system needs to be calmed down. It works by slowing down the growth of certain cells in your body, including cancer cells and overactive immune cells.
how_to_take: Methotrexate comes as a tablet you swallow, a liquid you swallow, or an injection given under the skin. Take the tablet or liquid by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. If you are giving yourself an injection, your doctor or nurse will show you exactly how to do it. Always use a new needle and syringe each time. Do NOT take methotrexate every day unless your doctor specifically tells you to — for most conditions like arthritis and psoriasis, you only take it ONCE A WEEK on the same day each week. Taking it more often can be very dangerous.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, weight, and kidney function. For rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, a common starting dose is 7.5 mg once a week, which may be slowly increased. For cancer, the doses and schedule are very different and will be set by your oncologist. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly. Never change your dose on your own. Mark your calendar with your weekly dose day to avoid mistakes.
missed_dose: If you miss your weekly dose and you remember on the same day or the next day, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next weekly dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose on your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist right away.
storage: Store methotrexate tablets and liquid at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. For auto-injectors or prefilled syringes, store in the refrigerator but do NOT freeze them. If refrigeration is not available, they can be kept at room temperature for up to 30 days. Keep all forms of methotrexate out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used needles safely in a sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking methotrexate — it greatly increases the risk of serious liver damage. Avoid taking ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other NSAIDs without talking to your doctor first, as they can increase methotrexate levels and cause serious side effects. Avoid aspirin unless your doctor tells you it is okay. Do not take vitamins or supplements containing folic acid in doses higher than what your doctor recommends without checking first. Avoid live vaccines (such as the flu nasal spray, shingles, or MMR vaccine) while on methotrexate — ask your doctor before getting any vaccine. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as methotrexate can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Avoid contact with people who are sick, as methotrexate can lower your ability to fight infections.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; unusual bleeding or bruising; blood in your urine or stools; black or tarry stools; signs of infection such as fever over 100.4°F (38°C), chills, or sore throat; shortness of breath or a new cough; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); mouth sores or ulcers; severe skin rash or peeling; sudden severe headache, blurred vision, or confusion; swollen lymph nodes; or if you think you may be pregnant. Also call your doctor if you feel unusually tired, have pain when urinating, or notice any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: For rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, it usually takes 3 to 6 weeks to start noticing improvement, and the full benefit may take 3 to 6 months. Do not stop taking it just because you do not feel better right away. For cancer treatment, your oncology team will monitor your response closely. Keep all your follow-up appointments and blood tests — these are very important to make sure the medicine is working and is safe for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use methotrexate if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects or miscarriage. Both women and men should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after stopping. Do not breastfeed while taking methotrexate. Kidney problems: Methotrexate is removed from your body by your kidneys. If your kidneys do not work well, the drug can build up and cause serious harm. Your doctor will check your kidney function regularly and may adjust your dose. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially effects on the liver, kidneys, and blood. Regular monitoring is especially important. Children: Methotrexate is used in children for certain conditions such as juvenile arthritis and some cancers, but doses are carefully calculated by weight and the child must be closely monitored.
